prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-01-29. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.04 |
| Retained earnings       | 87,663M |
| Current liabilities     | 38,980M |
| Current assets          | 40,596M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 18,677M |
| Total liabilities       | 111,269M |
| Total assets            | 130,169M |
| EBIT / operating income | 2,359M |
| Revenue                 | 12,717M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-01-29, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The reported metrics indicate a highly leveraged capital structure (equity only 14% of assets, liabilities/assets = 85%), minimal liquidity buffer (current ratio = 1.04), and an Altman Z-score of approximately 1.2 (distress zone). Offsetting factors are positive retained earnings, positive EBIT, and an EBIT margin near 19%, which together support a speculative-grade but not deeply distressed profile.
DECISION: BB-
(The rating reflects only the static 2026-01-29 snapshot and pre-2026 rating norms; forward-looking or qualitative adjustments are outside scope.)
